meta.title: Kiln Yoga, small yoga studio in Peckham
meta.description: A warm studio above a bakery in Peckham with just 14 mats. Slow flow, yin, a 4 week beginners course and pregnancy yoga on Saturdays.

rationale: A blush clay background, rounded corners and a soft serif make the page feel like the room itself: warm, handmade, unhurried. The beginners course is the featured service because it is the way in for new people, with the regular classes listed beside it. A hand-drawn kiln and loaf, a note from Mei and a short conversation about first visits carry the personality without stock yoga imagery.

props.headline: Yoga in a warm room above the bakery
props.sub: Fourteen mats, a wooden floor, big windows and the smell of bread in the mornings. Slow flow, yin, a beginners course and pregnancy yoga, taught by Mei and two other teachers.

photo.subject: The studio in morning light: wooden floor, big windows, a few rolled mats and blankets along the wall, no people, shot from the doorway

props.label: Classes
props.title: Small classes, for every kind of day
props.intro: With only 14 mats, the teacher knows your name and sees how you move. Book a single class, or take a class pass if you come often.

featured.name: Beginners course
featured.description: Four weeks, one class a week, with the same small group. We start with how to breathe and how to stand, then build up to a simple flow. No experience needed, no touching your toes required.

photo.subject: A beginners group of four or five people sitting on mats in a loose circle, laughing mid-conversation with Mei, warm window light

others.name: Slow flow
others.description: Unhurried movement linked with breath. Steady, a little strong, never rushed.

others.name: Yin
others.description: Long, quiet holds on the floor with bolsters and blankets. Good for tired bodies and busy heads.

others.name: Pregnancy yoga
others.description: Saturday mornings. Gentle movement, breathing and rest for every stage of pregnancy.

others.name: Single class or class pass
others.description: Drop in for one class, or buy a pass and use it across any of the classes above.

props.label: About
props.title: Hello, I'm Mei
props.text: I teach most of the classes here, with two other teachers who share the same slow way of working. I wanted a room that feels like a friend's front room, not a gym and not a showroom. So the studio is small on purpose: fourteen mats, a wooden floor, windows that let the day in. Some mornings the bakery downstairs sends the smell of fresh bread up the stairs. We have never minded.

photo.subject: Mei sitting cross-legged on the wooden studio floor, relaxed, looking toward the camera, in everyday clothes, natural window light

props.label: First visit
props.title: Never been to a class? Ask us anything

pairs.ask: I have never done yoga. Will I be lost?
pairs.answer: No. The beginners course is made for you, and in every class the teacher can reach every mat. Tell us it is your first time and we will look after you.

pairs.ask: What do I need to bring?
pairs.answer: Comfortable clothes and yourself. We have mats, blocks, bolsters and blankets in the studio. Bring your own mat if you prefer.
Choose a class, book a single place, or buy a class pass if you plan to come regularly. Classes are small, so booking ahead is wise.

pairs.ask: I am pregnant. Can I come?
pairs.answer: Yes, the Saturday morning class is for you. If you are unsure about anything, send us a message first and we will talk it through.

props.text: Come a little early, take your shoes off, and sit by the window. There is no rush here. See you on the mat. Mei

items.q: How many people are in a class?
items.a: No more than 14, because that is how many mats fit in the room. That keeps every class calm and personal.

items.q: Do I need to book in advance?
items.a: We recommend it. Places are limited to 14 mats, and the Saturday pregnancy class and the beginners course tend to fill first.
A bundle of classes you can use across slow flow, yin and the other classes on the timetable. Ask us for the current options.

items.q: Is the beginners course a good place to start?
items.a: Yes. It runs for 4 weeks with the same small group, so you learn the basics at an easy pace and get to know the room.
